Java's init/next/ENABLED specialized fallback branches evaluate the whole predicate and cast directly to `BoolValue`; the remaining generic Go `evalBool` helper is a compatibility compromise around that rough Java edge, not an invitation to invent friendlier non-Java messages.
- No-code audit note: `ByteUtils` and `ExSortUtils` were rechecked against Java after the missing-class inventory. Big-endian primitive encodings, Java `BigInteger` two's-complement byte arrays, fixed-width sign extension, short-read message typos, size-prefixed byte-array append paths, and the `ExternalSortable` BigInt specialization match the Java-visible stream formats.
- No-code audit note: state writer and liveness writer classes were rechecked against Java `IStateWriter`, `StateWriter`, `NoopStateWriter`, `ILivenessStateWriter`, `NoopLivenessStateWriter`, and `DotLivenessStateWriter`. Go intentionally folds the no-op/DOT/liveness interfaces into concrete writer structs while preserving Java dump names, no-op behavior, DOT liveness filename derivation, tableau-node labels, stuttering/dotted visualization, and seen/unseen successor labeling.
- No-code audit note: deterministic small utilities were rechecked after the trace pass. `ObjLongTable`/`SemanticNodeLongTable`/`LongObjTable` keep Java open-addressed slot-order enumeration with live key enumerators, `SetOfStates`/`SetOfLong` keep low-bit hash indexing, strict `next()` overrun behavior, Java signed collision-distance checks, and action-identity subsets, `SimpleCache` keeps the sentinel hit/miss counts and zero-fingerprint behavior, `JavaRandom` keeps aril accounting on `NextDouble`/prime stride selection, and `LongVec` keeps remove-by-swap plus reverse/pack/remove-last semantics.
- Bucket statistics utilities were rechecked against Java `util.statistics`: percentile clamping/NaN failure, literal `%n` string sections, fixed overflow buckets, dummy metrics, and HyperLogLog estimate casts match the Java-visible shape. Fixed-size statistics now also allow zero-sized construction like Java's zero-length array; inserting a sample then fails through the backing bucket access rather than a Go-only constructor guard.
- No-code audit note: `Strings`, base `Sequences`, and `Bags` were rechecked against Java after the trace/disk-queue pass. Their active override surfaces, Java-visible diagnostics, normalization quirks, and deliberate null-dereference wrapper errors are already aligned. The only noted representation edge is Java's ability to produce lone UTF-16 surrogate halves from `Tail`/`SubSeq` on supplementary-character strings; Go strings cannot preserve invalid UTF-16 code units without a larger `UniqueString` representation change.
- Parser-backed TLC semantic nodes now carry Java-style source locations through `SemanticNodeBase`. The TLC bridge attaches AST positions to converted definitions, expressions, and synthetic record/CASE/EXCEPT pair nodes, so action locations, debugger breakpoint matching, call stacks, coverage, and liveness/config diagnostics can use parser coordinates instead of falling back to `Unknown location`.
- `CallStack.String()` now renders frames in Java's source-location form (`Line ..., column ... to line ..., column ... in ...`) while `FingerprintException.GetTrace()` remains expression-text based like Java.
- Parser-backed set comprehensions now group tuple-bound variables into Java's single bounded-symbol-list shape for TLC, and mapped filtered comprehensions lower mechanically to `$SetOfAll(body)` over a filtered `$SubsetOf` bound. This removes the old bridge rejection for ordinary `{e(x) : x \in S, P(x)}` while preserving Java's `SetPredValue`/`SetOfAll` evaluator paths.
- Parser-backed function constructors now reuse the same Java-shaped bound grouping, so tuple-bound function parameters are passed to `FcnParams` as one bounded symbol list instead of one fake tuple-bound domain per variable.
- Parser-backed tuple-bound quantifiers intentionally re-collapse the parser's nested per-name chain into one Java-shaped bounded symbol list, so `\A <<x, y>> \in S : P` and `\E <<x, y>> \in S : P` reach TLC like SANY `OpApplNode` quantifiers instead of as chained one-variable quantifiers.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on simulator action-flow graph reduction unless touched: BASIC mode reduces action contexts by Java's action-definition `Location`, so all null-location actions collapse into the same bucket instead of being split by expression text.
- Action-flow graph FULL cluster ids use Java `Math.abs(String.hashCode())` semantics exactly, including the `Integer.MIN_VALUE` corner where `Math.abs` returns the same negative value.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on `TLCExt` hash/cache details unless touched: `TLCExt!TLCFP` is synchronized like Java, semantic node kinds use Java `ASTConstants` ids where mirrored, semantic-node hash follows `31*(31+kind)+uid`, value hash follows Java `Value.hashCode()`, and `TLCCache` state-level keys use Java's direct XOR expression.
- `TLCExt!PickSuccessor` non-boolean guard diagnostics must be emitted by the evaluating wrapper, where both the evaluated guard kind and original expression are available. Java reports the IF-condition message from `TLCExt.pickSuccessor`, not a generic helper type error.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on `TLCExt!Trace` unless touched: incomplete-state diagnostics, simulator trace `_action` records, initial-state singleton records, `INIT_UID` current-state reconstruction, and model-checker predecessor-trace-plus-current-state reconstruction match Java's `TLCExt.getTrace`/`RecordValue(TLCState, Action)` shape.
- `TLCExt!TLCGetOrDefault` deliberately differs from `TLC!TLCGet` for bad integer registers: Java does not reject negative indexes in this operator, it asks the register source and returns the supplied default when no value is found. Keep Go's default-return path for negative integers.
- `TLCExt!TLCCache` preserves Java's override/fallback split: constant and state-level expressions use cache paths, while action/temporal expressions return no override result and fall back to the pure TLA+ definition. Because Go also installs synthetic standard evaluating values, the synthetic `TLCCache` op definition must carry an identity body for Java-style `evalPure` fallback.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on TLC module `SortSeq`, `Permutations`, or `RandomElement` unless touched: insertion sort, permutation index/in-use generation, composite random element construction, set normalization, and interval/set `floor(nextDouble * size)` selection match Java.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on `Json`/raw string conversion unless touched: Go keeps printable `StringValue.UnquotedString()` separate from raw `StringValue.RawString()`, and module overrides now use raw `UniqueString` contents for JSON payload strings, file paths, model values, process arguments, and trace binary paths. `IOUtils!Serialize` NDJSON now follows Java's `Json.textSerialize` path by honoring `openOptions` and not creating parent directories.
- JSON conversion was re-audited against Java `tlc2.module.Json`: `ToJson`, `ToJsonArray`, `ToJsonObject`, `JsonSerialize`, `ndJsonSerialize`, deserialization, record/tuple/function-record/set conversion, function-record sequence detection, raw string keys/values, model values, compact output, IOUtils `openOptions`, and Java's guaranteed `charset` set all match the Java algorithmic shape.
- JSON object deserialization preserves Java/Gson duplicate-key behavior: the first key position is retained, but later occurrences replace that field's value. The helper map is lookup-only; output record ordering remains deterministic.
- `IOUtils!Serialize`/`Deserialize` must remain `@Evaluation`-style native overrides, not eager method values. Java evaluates serializer options first, then tries priority handlers (`Json` NDJSON before CommunityModules TXT for `Serialize`) and falls back to the TLA+ body only when no handler claims the format; Go mirrors this with `PriorityEvaluatingValue` and source-body attachment in the parser bridge.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on `_Possible` unless touched: Java's only native `_Possible` override is `_Counts`, which mirrors checker-else-simulator source selection before aggregating per-worker count records. `_Track`, `_CheckName`, and `_PrintCounts` are frozen standard-module TLA definitions; root `tlc_bridge.go` must not classify them as native overrides. See `TestPossibleStandardModuleKeepsOnlyCountsNative`.
- No-code bridge audit note: `_TLCTrace`/`_JsonTrace`/`_Possible` native override tables were rechecked against the frozen standard modules and Java annotations. Keep `_TLCTraceDeserialize`, `_TLCTraceSerialize`, and `_TLCState` native but LOCAL for `_TLCTrace`; keep only `_TLCState` native for `_JsonTrace`; and keep only `_Counts` native for `_Possible` while exporting the TLA-level helper definitions through the standard-member table.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on CommunityModules `Combinatorics` unless touched: Go now registers Java's `factorial` and `choose` overrides from `tlc2.overrides.Combinatorics`, backed by the already-ported `tlc2.util.Combinatorics` helpers. See `TestCombinatoricsCommunityModuleOverrides` and `TestCombinatoricsStandardModuleUsesNativeOverrides`.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on CommunityModules `Bitwise` unless touched: Go now registers Java's `And`/`Or`/`Xor` LOCAL helper overrides plus exported `Not` and `shiftR`; the root bridge exports only `&`, `|`, `^^`, `Not`, and `shiftR` for named instances, not the LOCAL helpers. See `TestBitwiseCommunityModuleOverrides` and `TestBitwiseStandardModuleKeepsLocalHelpersUnexported`.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on this CommunityModules override batch unless touched: Go now registers Java overrides for `DyadicRationals!Reduce` (LOCAL native only, not a named-instance export), `Functions!IsInjective`/`AntiFunction`/`FoldFunction`/`FoldFunctionOnSet`, `FiniteSetsExt!Quantify`/`kSubset`/`FoldSet`, and `BagsExt!FoldBag`. The fold argument order mirrors Java exactly: `FoldSet`/`FoldFunctionOnSet` call `op(element, acc)`, while `FoldBag` calls `op(acc, element)`.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on CommunityModules `CSV`/`GraphViz` unless touched: Go now registers Java's `CSVWriteRecord`, `CSVWrite`, `CSVRead`, `CSVRecords`, and `GraphViz!DotDiGraph`. CSV keeps Java's append/create writes, raw string paths/delimiters, regex delimiter splitting, signed 32-bit row count, and Java-style `%1$s` template placeholders; GraphViz DOT ids print signed `long` fingerprints.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on CommunityModules `Graphs`/`UndirectedGraphs` unless touched: Go now registers module-qualified native overrides for `SimplePath`, `AreConnectedIn`, `IsStronglyConnected`, and `ConnectedComponents`. These names collide across modules, so `standard_definitions.go` intentionally registers `Graphs!SimplePath`/`UndirectedGraphs!SimplePath` etc.; `tlc_bridge.go` aliases skipped source definitions and named instances to the module-qualified native values.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on CommunityModules `VectorClocks` unless touched: Go now registers Java's `CausalOrder` override. The implementation mirrors the Java/ShiViz-inspired phases: group by node, stable-sort each node log by vector-clock time, build parent edges from global-clock advancement, then emit zero-indegree roots; Go uses slice-backed deterministic host/parent tracking instead of randomized map iteration.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on the self-contained CommunityModules `SVG` overrides unless touched: Go now registers Java's `SVGElemToString`, `NodeOfRingNetwork`, and `PointOnLine`. `NodesOfDirectedMultiGraph` is deliberately not classified as native yet because Java delegates it to JGraphT/JUNG layout algorithms; leaving the TLA fallback is safer than inventing a non-conformant layout.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on CommunityModules `SequencesExt` unless touched: Go now registers Java's native overrides for set/sequence conversion, prefix/fold/search/remove/suffix/subsequence helpers, and the string replacement `@Evaluation` shortcuts. `ReplaceFirstSubSeq` and `ReplaceAllSubSeqs` now mirror Java's string-only native fast path and fall back to the parsed TLA+ definitions for non-string sequences.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on CommunityModules `Statistics` unless touched: Go now registers Java's `ChiSquare` override, including Commons Math's expected-count rescaling when expected and observed totals differ and the Java return convention of TRUE when the null hypothesis is not rejected at alpha.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on `tlc2/model` presentation structs unless touched: `TypedSet.parseSet` uses Java `String.split(..., 0)` trailing-empty behavior, `TypedSet` exposes/retains backing arrays and uses the Java empty-array default shape, trace-expression presence is null/non-null rather than non-empty, conjunctive descriptions include Java's optional ANSI wrappers, `MCError.toSequenceOfRecords` uses Java's original state-index comma rule, and `MCError.isLassoWithDuplicates` intentionally compares full lasso length against unique records from all but the final back-to-state marker.
- `MCState.parseState` intentionally keeps Java's leading-space-sensitive stuttering/back-to-state detection and fixed `label.substring(2, len-1)` action-label slicing. Do not trim labels there; Java output shape is part of the contract.
- `MCState.parseVariables` uses Java's exact `" = "` split and preserves the resulting raw name/value substrings; it does not trim around variable names or values, and extra separator pieces after the first value are ignored like Java's array indexing.
- `MCVariable.getValueAsStringReIndentedAs` follows Java `String.split("(\\r\\n|\\r|\\n)", 0)` behavior by dropping trailing empty split pieces before reindenting.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on trace-expression spec writer text generation unless touched: next-state/back-to-state construction now indexes like Java rather than silently tolerating malformed traces, the `TLC_TRACE_EXPLORER_JSON_UNCOMMENTED` property controls the JSON `ASSUME` comment exactly like Java, `indentString` drops trailing empty split parts like Java, and `TraceExpressionExplorerSpecWriter` iterates expression variables in Java `TreeMap` lexicographic order.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on generic spec-writer utilities unless touched: generated identifiers use Java's `AtomicLong(1L).incrementAndGet()` lifecycle with first suffix `2000`, and generated timestamp/modification-history dates use Java `Date.toString()`-style formatting rather than Go `time.String()`.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on `StatePrinter` unless touched: runtime/standalone/invariant/stuttering/back-to-state state printing follows Java, including diff-only state rendering, incomplete-state fingerprint `-1`, tool-mode back-to-state state messages, and the opt-in `tlc2.output.StatePrinter.overwrite` terminal reset property.
- Error-trace diff rendering must preserve Java `TLCTrace.printTrace` predecessor arguments, not simply use the previously printed state. Non-initial final error states are printed with a nil predecessor so `-difftrace` shows the full final state, while the initial-state shortcut passes the initial state as Java does.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on `ErrorTraceMessageRecorder` unless touched: back-to-state markers with a parseable ordinal finish the trace before target validation, matching Java's recorder ordering.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on worker successor ordering unless touched: `processSuccessorForWorker` mirrors Java `Worker.addElement` by checking `isGoodState` before attaching predecessor/action, then attaching predecessor/action before state/action constraints.
- Worker `getNextStates` failures are handled inside the iteration like Java `Worker.run`: wrapped successor failures and ordinary next-state exceptions are recorded through `doNextFailed` and do not escape as worker join errors. The worker still runs the deadlock/liveness/out-degree tail and lets the next `SDequeue` observe `finishAll()`, so deadlock/recorded-error outcomes return through the checker error code rather than a Go goroutine error.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on `TLCTrace.GetTraceAt` unless touched: local traces now carry the concrete `Tool` like Java `TraceApp` and reconstruct CheckImpl uncovered traces from disk fingerprints before falling back to the in-memory mirror.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on disk FPSet trace recovery unless touched: disk, off-heap, and multi FP sets now recover by streaming `trace.Elements()` like Java instead of iterating Go's in-memory trace mirror; memory FP sets still recover from their checkpoint files as Java does.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on worker deadlock tail ordering unless touched: deadlock detection now reports the error before liveness, but still runs Java's liveness graph update and out-degree sample before the worker stops.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on replay `doNextWithTool` constraint ordering unless touched: replay mirrors Java `ModelChecker.doNext` and does not attach predecessor/action before `isInModel`/`isInActions`; the normal worker functor path still follows Java `Worker.addElement`.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on disk state/byte queue checkpoint commit semantics unless touched: committed pool-file deletion and checkpoint rename failures now report Java-style errors instead of silently tolerating missing files in the committed range.
- Already audited recently; do not reintroduce a second production SCC algorithm in `LiveCheck`: `LiveCheck` now always uses Java's disk-graph/`LiveWorker` SCC path, creating a temporary metadir if a caller omits one. `LiveCheck1` remains separate because Java has that legacy checker too.
- `tlc2.tool.liveness.ILiveCheck.testing=true` selects the Java testing liveness path: build an `AddAndCheck` live checker over `tool.NoDebug()` and do not route it through the DOT state writer variant.
- `ConcurrentTLCTrace.getTrace(from, to)` now preserves Java's early one-state branch when `to` is initial or `from.equals(to)`. Do not let worker-file recovery return the `from` object for equal endpoints; Java wraps `to`.
- Already audited recently; do not flatten `LiveCheck.check0` back to a sequential loop: it now mirrors Java's queue-of-checkers worker orchestration, waits for all liveness workers, and lets liveness violations outrank worker errors.
- Already audited recently; do not route optional liveness statistics through structured TLC messages. Java prints `tlc2.tool.liveness.statistics` output directly to `ToolIO.out` after the final checker summary and before cleanup; Go mirrors that with stdout, including out-degree, in-degree, SCC-size buckets, and the SCC count line.
- Liveness temporal-property check completion uses the Java TLC human-readable runtime formatter, not Go's raw `time.Duration.String()`.
- Already audited recently; do not simplify action-composition intermediate collection: when `tlc2.tool.impl.Tool.cdot=true` is enabled, intermediate states must be collected through Java `StateVec.addElement(predecessor, action, state)` semantics, including predecessor/action attachment.
- Action-composition next-state generation must ignore the partial-state return from collecting the left-hand intermediates and return the original right-hand accumulator like Java `Tool.getNextStatesApplSwitch` does. The intermediate states themselves still feed the right-hand action; the return value is not the left collector's result.
- Already audited recently; do not loosen disk graph checkpoint commit errors: `DiskGraph.commitChkpt` now reports Java-style delete/rename failures.
- Already audited recently; do not replace `IntQueue` with a compacting Go slice queue: it now mirrors Java `MemIntQueue`'s circular buffer, growth rule, physical-index `popInt`, ring-ordered checkpointing, Java null-filename convention, and historical checkpoint error text.
- Already audited recently; do not replace LiveWorker SCC/postfix queues with Go slice queues: they now use the Java-shaped `IntQueue` long/int streams (`state`, `tidx`, `loc` and `state`, `parentLoc`).
- Already audited recently; do not replace `IntStack` with raw Go append growth: it now mirrors Java `MemIntStack`'s explicit backing array, 1024 minimum capacity, and 1.5x-or-plus-1024 growth rule. The no-arg `PeekLong` intentionally mirrors Java's top-cell-twice quirk; liveness formatter paths use the correct indexed `PeekLongAt`.
- Already audited recently; do not force LiveWorker SCC stacks to memory-only: `getStack` now mirrors Java's synchronized graph-size/free-memory threshold and selects `SynchronousDiskIntStack` when the liveness graph is large.
- LiveWorker final-check undone-node and final component-stack checks are Java `assert` statements, not production runtime failures. Go should not reject a run solely on those assertion-only conditions; keep hard errors only where Java would immediately fail through stack/node access anyway.
- Already audited recently; do not replace disk-graph liveness path BFS queues with Go slices: `DiskGraph.GetPath` and `TableauDiskGraph.GetPath` now use `IntQueue` record streams like Java.
- Already audited recently; do not loosen worker trace checkpoint commit errors: `Worker.commitChkpt` now reports Java's `Trace.commitChkpt: cannot delete ...` text for delete and rename failures.
- Already audited recently; do not add generic constrained-state writer fallbacks in worker successor processing: Java only writes the specific failed state/action constraints it finds.
- Already audited recently; do not make DFID worker stack sizing or stop/error handling friendlier than Java: worker arrays are sized from `Globals.DFIDMax`, init exhaustion goes through `DFIDModelChecker.SetStop(1)`, the inner DFS loop is keyed only by `isLeaf`, and panic recovery records a Java-style `GENERAL` worker failure.
- Already audited recently; do not run DFID workers synchronously from `ModelCheck`: `DFIDModelChecker.RunTLC` now mirrors Java's shared `AbstractChecker.runTLC` shape by starting the worker, running periodic checkpoint work, and emitting DFID progress/coverage while the depth search is active.
- DFID option presence is separate from depth value. Java treats `-dfid 0` as DFID mode with `TLCGlobals.DFIDMax == 0`; Go uses `Options.DFIDMode` for that presence bit, while positive `DFIDDepth` still enables DFID for programmatic callers. Do not restore the old negative-depth-as-unbounded fallback: Java's depth loop is exactly `for level = 2; level <= DFIDMax`.
- Already audited recently; do not move BFS progress/depth/coverage back into `DoPeriodicWork`: Java keeps checkpoint/liveness/periodic-condition work there and emits progress, depth cutoff, coverage, and waiting from `runTLCContinueDoing`.
- Already audited recently; do not loosen central `TLCTrace.commitChkpt` errors: failed delete or rename now reports Java's `Trace.commitChkpt: cannot delete ...` text.
- Already audited recently; do not add Go-wrapped causes or Go method names to checkpoint delete/rename errors in trace, liveness disk graph, queue, object stack/queue, memory FP set, or DFID FP-int set commit paths; they now use the Java `*.commitChkpt: cannot delete ...` strings.
- `MemStateQueue.commitChkpt` was separately rechecked after the disk queue pass: it must use Java's concrete `MemStateQueue.commitChkpt: cannot delete ...` text for both old-checkpoint delete failures and missing/failed `queue.tmp` renames. See `TestMemStateQueueCommitCheckpointErrorUsesJavaText`.
- Already audited recently; do not decode simulator packed Welford statistics with signed shifts: Java uses `>>> 32` for M2 and an unsigned low-32-bit mask for progress/statistics reporting.
- Already audited recently; do not skip simulator init progress messages: simulation now emits Java's computed-init progress and `TLC_INIT_GENERATED1` messages before normalizing/starting workers.
- Already audited recently; do not bubble simulator initial-state errors straight to the runner: Java prints incomplete-state, named invariant, or `TLC_INITIAL_STATE`/`GENERAL` diagnostics from the init loop, prints the simulator summary for exceptions, and returns that printed code.
- Already audited recently; do not return simulator no-init/no-init-after-constraint codes silently. Java returns `MP.printError(...)` for both branches after initial-state generation, so Go must print them before returning.
- Already audited recently; do not print raw unexpected simulator exception text. Java prints `MP.ECGeneralMsg("", exception)` for simulator init exceptions without a current state and for worker exceptions that are not liveness or TLC runtime-style errors; Go uses the shared Java-shaped general formatter for those fallbacks.
- Already audited recently; do not deep-copy or worker-stamp simulation states on selection/generation: Java uses the selected initial state directly and only attaches predecessor/action metadata to generated successors.
- Already audited recently; do not regenerate standard simulation successors through an intermediate `StateVec`: Java streams successors by passing the `SimulationWorker` as `INextStateFunctor` into `Tool.getNextStates`.
- Already audited recently; do not reintroduce simulator-wide random successor collection: Java standard simulation randomly selects an action first and then a successor from that action's generated states.
- Already audited recently; do not short-circuit `CheckImpl.checkTrace` on `false` results from state/reachability checks: Java calls those methods for reporting side effects and only thrown exceptions stop the loop.
- `CheckImpl` FP-set construction mirrors Java: the constructor's `FPSetConfiguration` belongs to the inherited `ModelChecker` FP set, while the coverage `coverSet` is created from the default FP-set factory with the `_cs` suffix.
- `CheckImpl` refinement failure output follows Java's plain `ToolIO` text for illegal transitions, implied-action violations, and invariant violations instead of routing those refinement-driver messages through generic TLC message-code formatting.
- Already audited recently; do not unbind failed `ENABLED` enumeration assignments between candidates: Java mutates the candidate successor state in place while enumerating `x' \in S`/`x' \subseteq S`.
- Already audited recently; do not count vector-path action coverage in individual checker callers: Java increments `action.cm` inside `Tool.getNextStates(action, state)` after generation.
- Coverage subtree collapse intentionally preserves Java `OpApplNodeWrapper.print`'s secondary-count self-comparison typo, and `UNCHANGED` coverage uses the live primary count in its max calculation even during cached subtree reporting.
- No-code audit note: coverage graph traversal still matches Java `CoverageHashTable`: non-recursive definitions are deliberately revisited through each call path, while recursive operator bodies are cut off only when the recursive definition is already on the active definition stack.
- Already audited recently; do not route direct `ModelChecker.DoNext` through the worker successor helper: Java's direct checker path checks model/action constraints before any eager predecessor/action attachment.
- Already audited recently; do not restamp DFID successors or action-label DFID state-writer edges in the depth loop: Java consumes the `StateVec` successor as returned by `Tool.getNextStates`, writes `allStateWriter.writeState(curState, succState, status)` without an action, and writes a stuttering self-edge before adding leaf states to liveness.
- Already audited recently; do not make `TLCStateMut.Copy` preserve predecessor/action in ordinary MC/DFID mode. Java ordinary `TLCStateMut.copy/deepCopy` drops predecessor/action, while simulation/debug/executor uses `TLCStateMutExt` and preserves that metadata; Go mirrors this with the `ToolMode`-driven state metadata switch in `SetTLCStateTool`.
- Already audited recently; do not preserve arbitrary `TLCError` codes in BFS `ModelChecker.doNextFailed`. Java preserves `EvalException` codes and treats stack overflow/out-of-memory/assertion as special, but leaves ordinary runtime-style failures as `GENERAL` with Java `ECGeneralMsg` text.
- Already audited recently; do not print every violated invariant/action property in continuation mode for one successor. Java prints the first violation it encounters for that successor and returns to the caller; the successor may still continue through the surrounding model-checking flow.
- Already audited recently; do not flatten next-state `CASE` coverage to the parent cost model. Java evaluates each next-state CASE guard and selected arm with `coverage ? cm.get(args[i]) : cm`; the `OTHER` fall-through uses `cm.get(args[alen-1])` exactly like Java, even though that is only identical to the `OTHER` arm when `OTHER` is last.
- Expression `CASE` coverage has the same Java arm-local shape: guards and selected arms use `cm.get(pairNode)`, and seeing an `OTHER` arm mutates the fallback cost model before the final `eval(other, ..., cm)` call.
- Already audited recently; do not pass the caller cost model when `ENABLED` recurses into a looked-up `LazyValue`. Java uses the lazy value's stored `lv.cm`, and Go mirrors that with `v.CM`.
- Already audited recently; do not lose function-lambda cost models in next-state function application. Java stores `cm` on `FcnLambdaValue`, evaluates lambda bodies through that `cm`, and next-state `f[x]` recurses into `fcn.body` with `fcn.cm`.
- Already audited recently; do not collapse Java `TLCState.Null` eval arguments to `EmptyState`. The Go variadic eval parser now assigns state arguments positionally, including explicit nil second states, so primed/lazy evaluation paths can mirror Java.
- Already audited recently; do not simplify `UNCHANGED` handling. Java emits warnings for changed variables, expands zero-arity operator/lazy aliases, uses distinct tuple pending-list order in `ENABLED UNCHANGED`, and uses a nested tuple cost model in next-state `UNCHANGED`.
- Already audited recently; do not unbind the original successor state after next-state assignment expansion. Java binds `resState`, assigns the return value of `getNextStates(...)` back into that local, and then unbinds that returned local for `x' = e`, `x' \in S`, `x' \subseteq S`, and missing-value `UNCHANGED`.
- Bounded `CHOOSE` must enumerate domains in Java `Enumerable.Ordering.NORMALIZED` order. Go preserves the efficient normalized `SUBSET`/`kSubset` enumerators and otherwise falls back to enumerating into a normalized `SetEnumValue`, matching Java's default `EnumerableValue.elements(Ordering.NORMALIZED)` algorithm.
- Bounded `CHOOSE` tuple binding now uses Java's `toTuple` conversion, allowing tuple-shaped finite functions while returning the original chosen element rather than the temporary tuple. Its non-enumerable check precedes normalization (operator values must report the CHOOSE error instead of panicking during normalization), and tuple-arity failures use Java's CHOOSE-specific diagnostic. Keep eager set-filter binding separate: Java's `$SubsetOf` branch directly casts tuple elements there. Three focused regressions failed before this fix and the full suite passes afterward.
- Already audited recently; do not make `FcnLambdaValue` copies preserve the cost model. Java's `FcnLambdaValue(FcnLambdaValue, ITool)` copy constructor does not copy `cm`; Go's `NewFcnLambdaValueFrom` mirrors that quirk even though fresh function constructors do store `CM`.
- Already audited recently; do not return immediately from `evalAppl` when a looked-up `LazyValue` is forced with `s1 == nil`. Java evaluates `lv.expr` into `val` and then continues through the normal OpDef/Value/OpValue dispatch, so operator values produced by the lazy expression still receive the original arguments.
- Already audited recently; do not drop operator-argument lambda cost models. Java constructs `OpLambdaValue(..., cm)` from `OpArgKind` and evaluates the operator body with that `cm`; copies of `OpLambdaValue` still do not copy `cm`, matching Java's copy constructor.
- Already audited recently; do not drop set-predicate cost models. Java constructs `SetPredValue(..., cm)`, copies that `cm`, and uses it when evaluating membership/enumeration predicates.
- `EvaluatingValue` fallback is intentionally different from `PriorityEvaluatingValue`: Java's plain wrapper calls `Tool.evalPure(opDef, args, ...)`, binding actual arguments lazily before evaluating the TLA+ body, while the priority wrapper falls straight through to `tool.eval(opDef.getBody(), ...)`. Preserve that split.
- Already audited recently; do not pass a debug/call-stack tool into final liveness checking. Java calls `liveCheck.finalCheck(tool.noDebug())`; Go now mirrors that final-check call just like periodic liveness calls.
- Liveness worker-failure diagnostics belong inside `LiveCheck.check0`: Java prints liveness worker `OutOfMemoryError` as `SYSTEM_OUT_OF_MEMORY_LIVENESS`, stack overflow as `SYSTEM_STACK_OVERFLOW`, and other causes as `GENERAL` before terminating. Go now emits the same diagnostic before returning the worker error to the checker.
- Liveness checker close was rechecked against Java `AbstractLiveChecker.close`: Java skips disk-graph close under `ModelChecker.VETO_CLEANUP` while still closing the writer. Go deliberately keeps the writer-close parity but closes disk graph files even when metadata deletion is vetoed, following the port rule that recovery artifacts are preserved without preserving likely file-handle leaks.
- `LiveCounterExampleException` mirrors Java's odd field shadowing: the subclass carries the counterexample while the embedded/base `LiveException` counterexample field remains nil. Callers that need the counterexample should check the subclass first, like Java `SimulationWorker.getCounterExample`.
- Liveness counterexample reconstruction has been re-audited against Java `LiveWorker.printTrace` and `LiveCheck.addNextStateTableau`. The disk-backed SCC path keeps Java's raw-vs-printable split: raw recovered states feed violated-property attribution and `CounterExample`, while alias-processed states are only printed. The safety-like path intentionally mirrors Java's odd alias-mutated trace before attribution/counterexample creation.
- Disk-backed `LiveWorker` SCC handling has been re-audited against Java `LiveWorker.checkComponent`, `printTrace`, `dfsPostFix`, and `bfsPostFix`. Go keeps the same trivial-component/stuttering fast path, component-table bucket scan, EA-action edge pruning for bidirectional-transition correctness, AE-state/AE-action/promise checks, SCC-size statistics, one-winning-worker error publication, raw-vs-printable lasso reconstruction, and Java-shaped postfix duplicate filtering. Java resets node pointer tables after a successful non-final `LiveCheck.check0`; Go performs the same successful-run reset checker-by-checker inside `LiveChecker.CheckSccs`, which is checker-local and currently preserves the visible effect.
- No-code audit note: the remaining `evalBool` callers in init/next/ENABLED equality, membership, subset, and property action-composition fallbacks follow Java's algorithmic shape: evaluate the whole predicate/action and use the boolean result after Java's branch-specific assignment fast paths. Java's source relies on direct casts there rather than adding a specialized diagnostic.
- Already audited recently; do not loop on normal/debug tableau disk graph semantics unless touched: Go has the ordinary `TableauDiskGraph` path and the Java `DebugTableauDiskGraph` DOT-after-mutation hook behind `tlc2.tool.liveness.LiveCheck.debug`. This is diagnostic output, not a different graph algorithm.
- Already audited recently; do not allow DFID liveness despite the dead code in `DFIDModelChecker`. Current Java asserts that DFID does not support checking liveness properties before model checking starts.
- Already audited recently; do not return from a failed DFID depth run without printing the DFID summary. Java's depth-search loop is inside a `finally` that prints summary on `runTLC` errors.
- Already audited recently; do not make DFID init continuation friendlier than Java. Initial invariants honor continuation mode, but implied-init violations always return `TLC_PROPERTY_VIOLATED_INITIAL`.
- Already audited recently; do not import BFS no-init errors into DFID. Java DFID sets the generated-init count to `states.size()`, trims accepted init arrays, and returns `NO_ERROR` even when no initial state survives model constraints.
- Already audited recently; do not make DFID next-state exceptions more precise than Java. Java DFID only treats stack overflow and out-of-memory as special; every other unexpected `doNext` failure is reported as `GENERAL` with the "computing the set of next states" context, even when BFS would preserve an `EvalException` code.
- BFS/DFID init error boundary: Java `DoInitFunctor` aborts init generation immediately for invariant violations, `Assert.TLCRuntimeException`, and `EvalException`, but records generic throwables and surfaces them after `getInitStates` finishes. The outer checker preserves only TLC-runtime-style error codes at this boundary; `EvalException` still aborts generation but reports through the Java generic initial-state exception path. Go mirrors this through `doInitFunctor.handleInitError` plus `initExceptionCode`; do not route all side-channel write/reporter errors through the immediate-abort path or preserve `EvalException` codes here.
- Worker next-state stop boundary: Java ordinary `Worker.addElement` does not return a graceful halt to `Tool.getNextStates`; stop-worthy successor failures call `doNextSetErr` and then throw `INextStateFunctor.InvariantViolatedException`, which the worker unwraps through `doNextFailed` while still running the deadlock/liveness/out-degree tail. Go mirrors this with a wrapped `errInvariantViolated` from `Worker.AddNextElement`.
- Initial-state action metadata must be read from the `ActionItemList` at the point the state is emitted, not before walking remaining all-assigned predicates. Java `ActionItemListExt.cdr()` mutates the tail's `prev`, so `acts.getAction()` after the walk can name the last checked init predicate; cacheing the action before the walk gives a different `TLCGet("action")`/debug record.
- Already audited recently; do not duplicate BFS-style invariant reporting in distributed TLC. Java routes distributed init and successor property checks through `TLCApp.checkState`, while deadlock and incomplete-successor checks happen in distributed next-state generation before fingerprinting.
- `CheckImplFile` deliberately keeps trace parsing behind `LoadTraceFunc`: the production SANY-to-TLC bridge is in the root `tlago` package and already imports `tlc`, so `tlc` must not import it. The root package now wires `NewCheckImplFileTraceLoader` and the `checkimplfile` CLI command; do not add a second parser in `tlc`.
- `TLAPlusExecutor` must force `Tool.Mode.Executor` and reset the state tool before generating its initial state. Java constructs `FastTool(..., Tool.Mode.Executor)`, which selects `TLCStateMutExt` so callable/predecessor/action metadata survives executor steps.
- State queue batch dequeue ownership differs by implementation: disk queues decrement `len` in `SDequeueMany`, while `MemStateQueue` and `StateDeque` decrement inside `dequeueInner`. This mirrors their single-dequeue paths; do not add a second decrement to the in-memory batch loops.
- State queue checkpoint suspension now mirrors Java's two-monitor shape: normal queue waiters use the queue condition, while checkpoint `SuspendAll` waits on a separate suspend barrier that workers signal only after all workers are waiting while work remains. Keep `finish`/`numWaiting` atomic so Go can perform Java's barrier rechecks without reversing the queue-lock/suspend-lock order.
- Randomization keeps Java's `RandomSubsetSet` helper available internally with `RandomSubsetSetProbability` diagnostics, but it is not registered as a standard operator or bridge export because frozen `Randomization.tla` does not define it.
- Base `Sequences.tla` does not define `Cons`; `Cons` belongs to `SequencesExt.tla`. The bridge standard-module members should therefore bind `SequencesExt!Cons` but not synthesize `Sequences!Cons`.
- Parser-backed liveness coverage already exists in top-level `tlc_liveness_parser_test.go`; it parses tiny TLA+ specs, builds a TLC tool, and drives `tlc.ParseLiveness`.
- Utility audit note: Java `MemObjectStack.beginChkpt` appears to checkpoint every other element because of an inner `i++`, which would corrupt multi-entry checkpoints; that class is used by legacy in-memory liveness helpers whose checkpoint methods are no-ops. Go keeps the working round-trip instead of importing that inactive corruption bug.
- Value utility audit note: Java `ValueVec.addElementAt` is a direct pre-sized slot fill plus count increment, not an insertion helper; sorted insertion belongs to `addElement1`, and `sort(noDup)` uses insertion over the sorted prefix with duplicate removal based on `compareTo == 0`. Go mirrors those splits and also enforces Java's `TLCGlobals.setBound` growth guard.
- `ValueVec.Search` now propagates comparison/equality errors through `SetEnumValue.Member` instead of treating them as absent elements. Sorted search calls `query.Compare(stored)`; unsorted search calls `stored.Equal(query)` like Java, rather than going through Go's query-first convenience `Contains` helper. This preserves asymmetric typed-model-value diagnostics and error precedence in membership, set reducers, and eager `UNION` combination. Verified by direct Java source comparison and the existing full Go suite; no new tests were written.
- `StateVec(TLCState[])` in Java retains the supplied array. Go `NewStateVecFrom` intentionally retains its supplied slice too; callers that need ownership must copy before construction.
- `SetEnumValue.elements()` must normalize in the enumerator construction path like Java, so enumeration itself sorts and removes duplicates for unnormalized sets.
- `SetEnumValue.compareTo`/`equals` must first convert the other value through Java's `Value.toSetEnum()` path; intervals and reducible set expressions compare as enumerated sets rather than failing as non-sets.
- `TupleValue.compareTo`/`equals` must first try Java's `Value.toTuple()` conversion on the other value and then fall back through the tuple's function-record view; tuple-compatible function records and the empty record compare as tuples.
- `RecordValue.compareTo`/`equals` must use Java's `Value.toRcd()` conversion path; in particular, the empty tuple converts to the empty record, while non-empty tuples do not convert to records.
- `CheckImpl.MakeStateSpace` must derive the root depth from `trace.getLevel(state.uid)` exactly like Java; do not fall back to the mutable state's cached level or an object-identity trace lookup for partial state-space extension.
- `CheckImpl.CheckReachability` deliberately calls `Tool.IsValidTransition(Tool.GetNextStateSpec(), ...)` even if the next-state action is nil, matching Java's unconditional `tool.isValid(next, s0, s1)` path instead of silently accepting every transition.
- No-code audit note: direct checker and worker successor ordering still mirrors Java `ModelChecker.doNext`/`Worker.addElement`: incomplete successors stop first, in-model/action constraints gate FP/trace writes, invariant checks only run for unseen successors, implied actions run for seen and unseen successors, and liveness successor sets collect every in-model seen or unseen successor.
- No-code audit note: Java's built-in override index contains only `TLCGetSet`, `TLCEval`, `TLCExt`, `Json`, `_TLCTrace`, `_JsonTrace`, and `_Possible`; Go's standard definitions still cover those annotations plus the older exact-name module native methods. Commented or unannotated Java helpers such as `TLC.FApply`, `TLC.FSum`, `RandomSubsetSet`, and `Bags.SubBag` are intentionally not registered as native overrides.
- The root `checkimplfile` command must recover `UniqueString` state from `-recover` before parsing/building the tool and must reset FP64 to index 0, mirroring Java `CheckImplFile.main` before `new FastTool(...)`.
- The root `checkimplfile` startup banner mirrors Java's exact concatenation: `TLC CheckImpl` immediately followed by `TLCGlobals.Version.get()`/`TLCVersion()`, with no extra inserted space.
- Ordinary `TLCStateMut.SetPredecessor`/`SetAction` must behave like Java's non-extended `TLCStateMut`: predecessor/action metadata is only preserved when the active tool mode selects the extended state class. Trace and distributed helper paths may attach private metadata explicitly when they are reconstructing or transporting trace records.
- Extended state metadata can also be forced with Java's `tlc2.tool.impl.Tool.TLCStateMutExt=true` property, matching `Tool.TLCSTATEMUTEXT_KEY`; `TLAGO_TLC_STATE_MUT_EXT=true` is the Go environment alias.
- Commit after each coherent chunk. Keep commit messages short and do not add authorship boilerplate.
- Current immediate note: the file-backed implementation checker is now reachable from the CLI, but it has not been exercised against an external simulator trace loop yet. It parses extensionless trace files by exact filename through `CheckSanySourceWithOptions`, converts root definitions with the production bridge, temporarily installs trace definitions while calling `Tool.MakeState`, and restores the main tool definition table afterward.

## Accomplished

- Documented TLC architecture in `tlc/TLC_ARCH.md`, including major Java subsystems, data structures, algorithms, correctness risks, and performance-sensitive areas.
- Established Go TLC package structure with central concrete implementations rather than a Java-style package/interface hierarchy.
- Ported core runtime scaffolding:
  - TLC globals, error codes, output/reporting helpers, registry/system-property helpers.
  - Semantic/action nodes, contexts, call stack, evaluation control, standard definitions, model config parsing.
  - Tool/spec processor skeletons with init/next/action/invariant/property/liveness collections.
- Ported substantial value layer:
  - primitive, model, tuple, record, function, set, lazy, operator, interval, stream, and set-constructor values.
  - Java fingerprinting/order behavior where it is known to affect traces, fingerprints, and diagnostics.
  - random enumerable value behavior folded into `random_generator.go`.
- Ported utility collections and IO helpers:
  - Java-style `ObjLongTable`, `LongObjTable`, `SetOfLong`, `Vect`, `LongVec`, `List`, `BitVector`.
  - byte utilities, buffered/random access files, BigInt/external sort helpers, deprecated BigSet shape.
  - concrete object stacks/queues, integer stacks/queues, synchronous disk int stack.
  - disk/byte/state queue pool readers/writers and state pool cleaner.
- Ported state machinery:
  - mutable states, state vectors, set-of-states, state info, state printer/writer, trace records.
  - state fingerprints, normalization hooks, model value permutations, symmetry setup.
- Ported fingerprint sets:
  - base FPSet APIs, NoopFPSet, MemFPSet, MemFPSet1, MemFPSet2, MultiFPSet, DiskFPSet, OffHeapDiskFPSet scaffolding.
  - Recent commit `e985339` replaced placeholder MemFPSet1/2 aliases with Java-shaped implementations.
- Ported liveness front end and graph structures:
  - AST-to-live conversion, `ParseLiveness`, `ProcessLiveness`, PEM/order/tableau structures.
  - `TBGraph`, `TBGraphNode`, particles, promises, possible error models.
  - BEGraph, graph nodes/transitions, disk graph and tableau disk graph checkpoint/recovery/traversal basics.
  - Recent commit `ca4060d` fixed disk graph `AddNode` to honor recovered file pointers instead of always seeking EOF.
- Ported major checker/simulator scaffolding:
  - Model checker/DFID/check-impl/worker outlines and selected worker behavior.
  - Simulator and SimulationWorker with standard, debug-exploration, RL, and RL-action modes folded into one concrete worker plus mode flags.
  - Simulator now creates default per-worker live checks when Java would check liveness, using worker-specific graph directories under the simulator metadir.
  - Simulator now has a Java-style progress reporter for simulation progress, coverage/action-flow updates, and `_PERIODIC` false termination.
  - Simulator now prints Java-shaped worker-error behaviors and final simulation summaries (`TLC_STATS_SIMU`) with coverage/action-flow finalization.
  - Exploration/debug simulation now preserves Java's `ExplorationWorker.halt()` behavior: debugger step-out can command the next-state functor to halt, while state generation separately polls the halted flag.
  - `CheckImpl` now mirrors more of Java's visible control flow: partial-state-space start/completion/failure messages, illegal-transition standalone state printing, implied-action standalone state printing, side-effect-only `checkTrace` false results, and Java-shaped `CheckImplFile` trace polling output.
  - Worker trace checkpoint commit now fails when the worker `.tmp` checkpoint cannot be renamed, matching Java's `Worker.commitChkpt()` behavior instead of silently ignoring a missing checkpoint.
  - Core TLC message formatting now covers Java-shaped run/progress/statistics/checkpoint/coverage strings for the message codes already emitted by the Go checker, simulator, and coverage paths.
  - The TLC runner now supplies Java-shaped startup mode banner parameters and finished-runtime strings for BFS, DFID, and simulation runs.
  - BFS model checking now follows Java's recover-before-fresh-start ordering and preserves the `TLC_LIVE_FORMULA_TAUTOLOGY` guard.
  - BFS model checking now emits Java's final safety progress snapshot immediately before final liveness checking.
  - Worker liveness failures now follow Java's call-stack replay path for `EvalException`/stateful runtime failures and preserve the original error after replay.
  - `ModelChecker.doNextFailed` now preserves `EvalException` error codes/parameters and Java's keep-call-stack behavior for known fatal/system-like TLC errors.
  - Initial-state error handling now preserves Java's `DoInitFunctor` split: expected TLC/evaluation failures abort through the outer diagnostic path, while generic init-side failures are recorded on the functor and surfaced after `getInitStates`.
  - Checkpoint recovery now rebinds the checker metadir and all trace fragments to `FromCheckpoint`, matching Java's `FileUtil.makeMetaDir(..., fromChkpt)` behavior for resumed runs.
  - BFS `RunTLC` now follows Java's `keepCallStack` return convention and `ModelCheck` replays next-state failures with `CallStackTool` before final summary output.
  - BFS `RunTLC` now follows Java's periodic-loop ordering: an initial worker grace wait, then `DoPeriodicWork`, then progress/depth/coverage continuation, then the progress-interval wait.
  - Initial-state exceptions now print the Java-shaped init failure message and replay init generation with `CallStackTool`, including fingerprint-exception handling.
  - Periodic-work liveness/periodic-condition failures now leave the state queue suspended for outer termination, matching Java's error-return path.
  - DFID clean termination now reports success instead of `GENERAL`, and DFID next-state replay can run through `CallStackTool` like Java's `DFIDModelChecker`.
  - DFID liveness requests now fail with Java's issue-548 guard instead of entering the obsolete liveness body.
  - DFID init now prints Java-shaped invariant/implied-init diagnostics and replays init exceptions with `CallStackTool`.

  - Liveness `Check`/`FinalCheck` now honor Java's `LNCheck` gates: periodic checks obey `DoLiveness`, and final checks skip when liveness checking is `off`.

  - Liveness DOT/debug writer calls now mirror Java's disk-backed liveness paths: initial states are written for non-tableau/tableau checkers, non-tableau transitions carry bit-vector labels and seen/unseen status, tableau cross-product edges are emitted on insertion, and recursive done-expansion writes dotted edges for generated state successors.
  - Legacy in-memory `LiveCheck1` is now ported as a concrete Go struct: trace graph construction, incremental BE/BT graph updates, Tarjan SCC passes, PEM subcomponent checking, and liveness error trace reconstruction are present. `BEGraphNode` now preserves tableau identity so Java's BT-node equality semantics are not collapsed to state fingerprints.
  - Simulator workers now mirror Java's liveness selection: default per-worker checks use concrete `LiveCheck1` with a shared error flag, while disk-backed simulation liveness is only selected via the Java-style `tlc2.tool.Simulator.experimentalLiveness` property or `TLAGO_SIMULATOR_EXPERIMENTAL_LIVENESS`.
  - Liveness check/worker/error-trace skeletons with concrete disk graph fields.

  - Distributed worker checking now mirrors Java's `TLCApp`: generated successors are checked for deadlock and complete assignment before fingerprinting, and invariant/implied-init/implied-action checks are centralized in the worker-shaped `checkState` path.

- Core Json.textSerialize NDJSON stream slice: authoritative source is core
src/tlc2/module/Json.java, whose evaluating override is absent from Community
Json.java. Earlier general claims that JSON stream writing always replaces
malformed input are superseded: Files.newBufferedWriter supplies a CharsetEncoder
with REPORT actions. Ordinary OutputStreamWriter/FileWriter constructors still
replace. String's optimized strict Files codec and the REPORT encoder differ:
UTF-8 unmatched surrogates are malformed here, and Latin-1 supplementary pairs
report unmappable length two. Existing exhaustive String-codec observations remain
valid for their separate methods.

The evaluating callback retains options/format, payload conversion and destination
order. Converted record/tuple objects are retained once rather than reconverting
after destination evaluation. Required tuple/string/element casts remain outside
the source catch; native null dereferences retain their exception families, without
manufacturing VM helpful detail text. RecordValue.apply now returns a present
null field directly, mirrors the single source catch and accepts the represented
StringValue subclass. Missing fields retain their existing failure.

The actual Linux stream opens before JSON node conversion and encoding, reusing
the prior source-derived path/open-option/delete behavior. BufferedWriter retains
8192 UTF-16 units, while StreamEncoder separately retains 8192 bytes, REPORT
surrogate/unmappable errors, UTF-16 BOM state and leftover surrogate state.
Source buffer flip/clear order survives failed writes; partial file content is
retained. Close flushes character/byte buffers and closes the file despite errors;
primary failures retain suppressed close failures, including nested suppression,
and Json wraps caught Exception as RuntimeException(cause). Error stays outside
that catch. Source JDK 21 bytecode was inspected for the platform-thread buffer
and close paths; virtual-thread-specific buffer sizing is not represented here.
Throwable suppression uses shared synchronized storage and stack rendering places
suppressed failures before causes, preserving indent/order. This is the internal
resource-close path, not a claim of the complete public Java Throwable API.

Gson JsonElement string rendering now uses its actual non-HTML-safe escaping:
control escapes, U+2028/U+2029 escapes, and unchanged remaining UTF-16 units,
including unmatched surrogates until stream encoding. The represented debugger
StringValue subclass follows the string branch. Unsupported values retain
IOException with the Java class name; null retains NullPointerException.

- Ordinary core Json.serialize/ndSerialize FileWriter slice: both validate payload
before dereferencing the path; Json.serialize checks the converted shape but
serializes the original value, while ndSerialize retains the converted tuple.
Files open/truncate before node conversion. File.mkdirs' return is ignored;
no parent-creation error replaces the subsequent native open failure. Ordinary
try-with-resources retains the primary Exception/Error without the NDJSON
RuntimeException wrapper, adding close failures as suppressed failures.
The existing BufferedWriter/StreamEncoder carrier now represents replacement
coding for FileWriter as well as REPORT coding for Files.newBufferedWriter.
Replacement preserves surrogate-pair consumption and separate character/byte
buffers; UTF-8/ASCII/Latin-1 use question-mark replacement, UTF-16 variants U+FFFD.

Linux java.io.File normalizes separators without resolving dot components;
its native filename encoding replaces malformed UTF-16, unlike NIO's strict
UnixPath. FileOutputStream keeps the original normalized UTF-16 logical path
in FileNotFoundException(path + native reason), including malformed units.
NUL yields FileNotFoundException("Invalid file path"); empty native paths retain
ENOENT rather than addressing the current directory. Files use 0666 and directory
creation 0777, filtered by umask. mkdirs first tries the raw path, then canonical
parent creation. Canonicalization resolves an existing prefix and normalizes
unresolved dot components; hard failures in a parent, including symlink loops,
cannot be discarded. The shared Unix separator normalizer is reused by TXT.
Other native File providers and native filename charset discovery remain pending;
the non-Linux fallback does not establish those source semantics.

Default FileWriter charset now retains a frozen initial file.encoding value
with cached resolution, separate from later runtime System property mutation.
The Go command's startup -D processing supplies the initial value. JDK 21
Charset/FileWriter/FileOutputStream/File/UnixFileSystem bytecode was inspected.
Six guaranteed charsets and their aliases are represented; unknown initial names
fall back to UTF-8 as the standard provider does. Extended standard/provider
charsets and COMPAT/native locale discovery remain unported; these observations
do not establish those settings. The initial/default charset carrier is now
available for the later reader/process byte-decoding port.

Json's three synchronized static writer methods share the existing concrete
reentrant monitor. The evaluating NDJSON callback acquires it before evaluating
options, allowing same-thread recursive JSON writes while other writers wait;
ordinary reader/string methods remain unsynchronized as source. This resolves the
static-monitor gap noted in the previous JSON slice without inventing an interface.

## Fingerprint checkpoint catch and EOF fidelity (October 8, 2026)

Compared Java FPSetManager.chkptInner/Checkpoint.run and TLCServer checkpoint
order with Go. The source runs each checkpoint helper synchronously, catching
only IOException and printing through ToolIO. Go incorrectly swallowed every
returned error and printed directly to os.Stdout. The manager now invokes the
endpoint with the existing checked/unchecked panic boundary, catches I/O only,
and returns an unchecked failure immediately. Begin failure skips commit;
I/O failure continues to the next grouped server; fatal local failures still
escape. Source checkpoint/commit/recover ordering and grouped-entry behavior
are unchanged. No asynchronous checkpoint or rollback policy was invented.

MemFPSet, MemFPSet1 and MemFPSet2 commit rename/delete failures now retain their
source IOException category, allowing the manager and native endpoint to classify
them accurately. The EOF audit exposed another shortcut: MemFPSet and MemFPSet2
accepted a truncated fingerprint record as normal termination. Source first
checks BufferedDataInputStream.atEOF, then catches an EOF during readLong.
Go now uses one lookahead reader and the unbuffered/no-handle value reader for
that same fixed-width stream. Clean EOF returns normally. A partial record
returns the original SYSTEM_DISK_IO_ERROR_FOR_FILE/checkpoints runtime failure
for MemFPSet and `MemFPSet2.recover: failed.` IOException for MemFPSet2.

versus unchecked errors, exact ToolIO warning and source order, fatal propagation,

record. Native TCP corruption recovery must propagate its non-I/O failure rather
than report an unavailable server. Existing valid native checkpoint round trip
and original manager methods retain their assertions.

## October 8, 2026: model scalar types and floating-point bit preservation

Audited worker next-state processing and model payloads against pinned Java.
ModelValue.data is an ordinary non-transient Object, so source boxed Byte,
Short and Float are transferable. The native codec rejected the corresponding
int8, int16 and float32 values. Added those explicit scalar kinds and narrow
integer decode bounds. New gob cases reproduce the rejection before the fix
(7885 terminal status 1, 0.011 seconds).

The first fix exposed negative-zero loss: gob omits struct float fields that
compare equal to zero. Both the new float32 and existing float64 path therefore
need integer IEEE bit patterns rather than a DTO float64 field. Initial scalar
selection fails at negative zero in 0.016 seconds (29508 terminal status 1);
initial TCP/graph selection confirms the same failure at both boundaries in
0.023 seconds (terminal status 1). Replaced DataFloat with DataFloatBits for
both float widths and validate float32's uint32 representation before decoding.

New checks retain exact native types, integer extrema and floating-point bits
for positive/negative zero, ordinary fractions, maxima, smallest subnormals,
infinities and NaN. The TCP worker checks request values before echoing them,
then the caller checks every result value. Narrow out-of-range integer and
float32 bit payloads must fail. No enabled direct upstream method covers this
native boundary; supplemental checks add no original-method completion credit.

### October 8, 2026: interning recovery owns its lock before file I/O

Checkpoint sequence audit confirms Java and Go order queue, trace, intern and
fingerprint commits identically. The isolated after-trace/before-intern process
interruption still lacks a faithful deterministic boundary; it was not replaced
by a timing race, production hook or different failed-intern-commit scenario.
The related interning audit found a concrete source mismatch: InternTable.recover
is synchronized for its entire method, but Go opened/read the checkpoint header
before acquiring the interning mutex. Concurrent token allocation could occur
during that read and then be overwritten by the restored token counter.

Recover now acquires the existing native mutex before file opening/header reads
and retains it through token publication and replay. Deferred unlocking covers
open/header/replay failures. The source has no direct InternTable recovery test;
new short Linux FIFO checks prove lock ownership at a blocked header read using
the actual reader/writer open handshake, without sleeps or production hooks.
Complete and truncated headers verify lock release and the next allocated token;
truncation leaves the prior counter intact. This is native supplementary coverage,
not original-method completion credit.

## October 12, 2026: Java queue-checkpoint crash-boundary confirmation

Compare the pending `DiskStateQueue.BeginChkpt` writer-drain proposal with the
unchanged Java queue and worker sources. Both Java and Go `beginChkpt` methods
publish queue metadata without waiting for a pending pool write. Both writer
threads drain pending work after `finishAll`, but neither checkpoint method
establishes that boundary before a process crash.

Build a bounded external probe against the frozen `tla2tools.jar`, restricted to
CPUs 0-7. Enqueue 16,385 valid states with 64 integer values apiece into the
source 8,192-state queue, commit a checkpoint and call `Runtime.halt(0)` at the
published marker. Pool `0` is complete at 2,670,592 bytes, pool `1` stops at
2,547,712 bytes and a fresh JVM fails recovery with `EOFException`. An otherwise
identical control that waits one second before checkpointing writes both pool
files at 2,670,592 bytes and recovers all 16,385 states. Pool `0` and
`queue.chkpt` hashes are identical across both runs; only pending pool `1`
differs. The exact probe, commands, artifacts and hashes are retained under
`.codex-gotmp/java-checkpoint-crash/`.

This resolves the earlier Java host-stop uncertainty: the prepared writer wait
fixes an upstream crash-consistency defect rather than restoring source parity.
It remains uninstalled pending explicit authorization for that divergence. No
long workload or background process ran, no test assertion changed, and the
separate checkpoint error-formatting decision remains untouched. The full gate

## October 12, 2026: StateQueue finish monitor order

Correct the remaining production divergence identified by the bounded
StateQueueJPF monitor audit. Java's synchronized `finishAll` sets finish,
notifies queue waiters and acquires/notifies the suspension monitor before
releasing the queue monitor. MemStateQueue, StateDeque, DiskStateQueue and
DiskByteArrayQueue previously released the queue monitor before that suspension
signal. Move each signal inside the queue-monitor critical section, preserving
the source queue-to-suspension lock order and every existing pool-finish action.

The focused ordinary queue selection passes normally and with `-race`. The exact
StateQueueJPF and DiskStateQueueJPF workload translations behind `tlc_verify`
also pass normally and with focused `-race`. This corrects production monitor
ordering but does not claim exhaustive scheduler/JPF completion credit. All
commands and children share CPUs 0-7.


## October 12, 2026: StateQueue stuck-resume wake order

Correct all four concrete queues to retain Java `StateQueue.resumeAllStuck`
ordering and observations. Java first observes stop and wakes the suspension
monitor when stopped. It then independently observes non-stopped, nonempty and
waiting state before waking queue consumers. The Go implementations previously
captured one queue-state snapshot and performed the queue-consumer wake first.
They now release the queue monitor after reading stop, wake the suspension
monitor if required, and reacquire the queue monitor for the independent
consumer-wake recheck.

The focused ordinary queue and distributed wake selection passes normally and
with `-race`. The original in-memory StateQueueJPF workload passes normally, and
both StateQueueJPF and DiskStateQueueJPF workload translations pass with focused
`-race`. The disk workload passed normally under file-only tracing but failed
twice at normal speed in `StatePoolReader`; it does not call `ResumeAllStuck`, so
that scheduler-sensitive native pool-worker issue remains separate and open.
All packages compile offline. This production ordering correction claims no
exhaustive scheduler/JPF completion credit. All commands and children share
CPUs 0-7.


## October 12, 2026: pool reader post-wait finish check

Correct StatePoolReader and ByteArrayPoolReader to check `finished` immediately
after each condition wait, as both Java reader loops do. Retain the native
pre-wait check as well so a reader goroutine first scheduled after the finish
broadcast cannot miss shutdown. This prevents a competing readability wake
from bypassing a finish notification before the reader reacquires its lock.

The focused original disk-pool writer and concrete queue tests pass normally
and with `-race`; both verify-tag queue workloads pass in a focused race run.
Repeating the original disk workload 100 times normally still produces nine
pool-reader EOF exits through a distinct source workload defect. Its appended
`DummyTLCState(fp)` retains `INIT_UID=-1`, contrary to `writeLongNat`'s
nonnegative precondition. A schedule that publishes that pool before the reader
is marked finished reads four `0xff` UID bytes and then reaches EOF while
requesting the encoded long's second word. Preserve that source data and the

| Source operation | Retained scheduling boundary |
| --- | --- |
| suspendAll initial queue section | stop/count publication followed by release before checkpoint acquisition |
| suspendAll checkpoint section | separate finish read and count recheck; wait releases checkpoint monitor atomically |
| isAvail worker barrier | separate waiting increment, last-worker decision, nested checkpoint acquisition, notify/release and queue wait |
| waking worker | queue monitor reacquisition, waiting decrement and finish/loop decision |
| dequeue/enqueue/finish | separate synchronized calls; finish publishes before waiting for nested checkpoint monitor |

Queue-protected payload/local-loop operations can be grouped because the only
payload pointer is fixed, competing workers need that queue monitor, and main
never reads the payload or iteration counters. Waiting increments remain
separate because main may observe them under the other monitor. Grouping the
checkpoint count-check and wait does not erase a notification: the checkpoint
monitor excludes notifiers until wait releases it. Monitor barging remains
possible for all runnable actors. Starting all actors as runnable covers the
source start order because main and earlier workers may remain unscheduled
until later threads start; the parent makes no further shared mutations.

## October 19, 2026: native test paths under symlinked temporary directories

Investigated the reported remote checkpoint, recovery, invariant-close and
fingerprint-startup failures by source analysis only, as requested. The empty
checkpoint syscall trace and successful promotion despite an intended EIO are
consistent with a symlink in the temporary directory path. strace's
`pathtrace_select_set` retains the supplied path and adds its `realpath` only
when that call succeeds; an uncreated `job.fp.tmp` cannot be resolved. Its
descriptor filter compares the resolved `/proc/<pid>/fd` path literally, so
that checkpoint's writes and close escape both tracing and injection. Existing
recovery and scan files can be resolved by strace, but their assertions still
compared the original directory spelling with the resolved `-yy` output.
Source: https://github.com/strace/strace/blob/master/src/pathtrace.c.

Added the shared test helper `canonicalNativeTestDirectory`, which resolves an
existing directory and makes it absolute before a checkpoint filename is
appended. All six path-filtered strace suites now use that spelling for both
filters and output assertions, including the unreported MemFPSet1 write cases
and the previously partially corrected recovery-close cases. Original paths
still reach application code; fault positions, syscall counts, partial-content
checks, cleanup assertions and checkpoint promotion rules are unchanged.

Consolidated both `/proc/self/fd` enumerations in `nativeTestDescriptorsUnder`.

## October 19, 2026: validate early safety violations during trace replay

Read the user's `/Users/jaten/tlago/log` without modifying it. The failing
`TestJavaSafetyDumpLoadTraceJSONAutoWorkers` dumps an 11-state DieHard trace
with 18 workers and replays an 8-state trace with one worker. Their first seven
states match. From state 7 (small bucket 2, big bucket 5), pouring big to small
produces small bucket 3, big bucket 4, water to pour 1: the same violating state
that appears at dump state 11. The dump first takes an empty/pour/fill detour.
The existing assertion incorrectly requires replay state 8 to be the dump's
nonviolating empty-big state.

This matches the previously documented unchanged-Java prefix failure. Both
Java Worker.addElement and native processSuccessorForWorker check invariants
on successors rejected by a state constraint; -loadTrace installs precisely
such a constraint. Multiworker exploration can retain a nonminimal predecessor
chain, so replay can encounter a violating successor before the dump's detour.
Suppressing that invariant would change TLC behavior. Java source reference:
https://github.com/tlaplus/tlaplus/blob/master/tlatools/org.lamport.tlatools/src/tlc2/tool/Worker.java.

Corrected the shared dump/load harness for the user's reported intermittent
failure. For differing dump/load worker settings and a safety result, only the
last replay state may use the alternative check, and only when the actual replay
tool rejects it under its model constraints. Every preceding state still uses
the original exact or ALIAS-intersection comparison, with all ordinal and length
checks retained. The terminal check uses raw pre-ALIAS states, evaluates the
real transition relation, requires exactly one matching invariant name in both
runs, and evaluates that invariant as true on the predecessor and false on the
successor. A broken transition, unrelated violation, earlier state mismatch,
constraint-accepted mismatch or liveness mismatch still fails. The same helper
covers JSON, binary and existing alias variants; no new scenario was invented.

This is an explicit correction to the upstream test's prefix assumption,
superseding the earlier instruction in port notes to retain that known faulty
assertion. Production code, flags, worker counts, fixtures and skip conditions

### October 19, 2026: upstream off-heap flusher lifecycle correction

Reviewed local upstream commits `4c83d5e63`, `8c9533d44`, and `210df3af8`
against `JAVA_BUG_FOUND.md` and our fallback implementation. Upstream is more
complete: it prevents temporary concurrent flushers from replacing the inherited
sequential default, sizes final-check preparation and scanning to initialized
disk readers, and shuts down preparation executors even without a merge.
Our fallback prevented stale reuse on successful paths but retained stored
executor state and used the unrelated global worker count for final checking.

Ported operation-local selection; removed the stored concurrent flusher and
completed-flush workaround. Inherited invariant/recovery flushing is always
sequential. `CheckFPs` uses `numThreads` from initialization and shuts down its
local preparation executor via defer, including panic paths. The separate scan
still joins all tasks. Go invokes bounded goroutines and joins them per batch;
there are no persistent idle executor threads, unlike Java. The existing
in-memory-only closest-pair approximation remains unchanged.

Ported all six upstream `OffHeapDiskFPSetFlusherReuseTest` methods. The Java
field-type assertion is represented by removal of the field and a default-flush
control; the thread-leak check observes Go goroutines, with a one-second bound
instead of an unbounded join. Existing selector boundary checks remain. Focused
regressions pass in 0.020 seconds; the 16 original insertion/eviction methods
and two original merge controls pass in 0.034 seconds. Commands use
`taskset -c 0-7`, an explicit short test selection and a 10-second timeout.
No Java or long distributed workload was launched. Updated the bug report
with the upstream resolution while retaining its historical report.

The same focused flusher regressions pass under `-race` in 1.160 seconds.
